findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine is observed to be testing at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine sanitizer. A follow up is scheduled for 8/14/2026 to ensure that the dish machine has been serviced and is testing at a label-recommended concentration of Chlorine sanitizer. Ensure that the dish machine is being regularly tested and serviced if not at a label-recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Cheese sauce and beans were both probed to be at 113F in the hot holding steam table. Both of these food items are canned products. CORRECTED- The hot holding steam table was only on a setting of 2 and the PIC increased the setting of it. The cheese sauce later probed to be at 139F and the beans probed to be at 138F. Proper hot holding temperatures were discussed with the PIC. Ensure that TCS food in hot holding is being held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There are rodent droppings observed to be in the gap between the wall and the walk-in cooler. There are also rodent droppings observed to be in the corner by the walk-in freezer and throughout the storage area near Little Yellow Wagon’s storage. A follow up is scheduled for 4/17/2026 to ensure that rodent droppings are being cleaned to allow for proper monitoring of the pest situation. Ensure that pest control is routinely treating the facility for rodents and that droppings are regularly being cleaned to allow for monitoring.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.
